Rejecting omitted masks **breaks this API’s contract**: Books v2 explicitly makes the mask optional and selects only mutable fields populated with nonempty values ([contract.json](/tmp/tal-skills-fieldmask-native-2026-10-15-r02/trials/source08-microservice-v3-aip134-omitted-mask-01/workspace/project/contract.json:10)).

Each request independently starts from the original resource. These are **expected contract outcomes**, not observed execution:

| Request | Selected mutable fields | Resulting resource |
|---|---|---|
| `omitted-mask` | `title` | `{"name":"publishers/P1/books/B2","title":"New","author":"Lin","rating":5}` |
| `explicit-author-reset` | `author` | `{"name":"publishers/P1/books/B2","title":"Old","author":"","rating":5}` |
| `wildcard-replacement` | `title`, `author`, `rating` | `{"name":"publishers/P1/books/B2","title":"New","author":"","rating":0}` |

For the omitted mask, `author: ""` does not select author; the absent rating also remains unselected. Both stored values survive. Explicitly selecting author writes its supplied default, intentionally clearing it. The wildcard requests full replacement, so author becomes empty and the absent rating takes its declared default, `0`. `name` identifies the resource and remains unchanged throughout.

The reviewer’s general Protobuf rule does not override this provider’s expressly adopted AIP 134 dialect. Rejecting the supported v1 request before the update implementation would turn a valid title update into a rejection, leaving the original resource unchanged. The proposed omission-only gate would still accept the explicit reset and wildcard requests. Mandatory masks would require a breaking-contract migration with coexistence for supported callers; recommending explicit masks for clear intent can coexist with the current optional-mask contract.
